claim_text: As of Redis 7.0 there are still legitimate use cases that require writable replicas.
The Kubernetes exec example probes more often than the HTTP example.
The number of SQLite schema objects can be capped with SQLITE_LIMIT_SCHEMA since version 3.45.0.
The Redis master remembers the last ping time from each replica.
If two Redis instances share a replication ID with offsets 1000 and 1023, the first is 23 bytes of replication stream behind.
A 281 terabyte SQLite database is large enough to actually reach the theoretical row limit.
Repeatable Read takes its snapshot at the first non-transaction-control statement of the transaction.
Reconnecting Redis replicas use PSYNC with their old replication ID and offset to resume incrementally.
PostgreSQL's default isolation level can be changed with the default_transaction_isolation parameter.
A web browser could use sqlite3_limit() to keep its internal history database unconstrained while tightly limiting databases created by downloaded JavaScript.
Once the startup probe succeeds once, the liveness probe takes over.
Under Repeatable Read, successive SELECTs in a transaction see the same data.
An SQLite host parameter like ?1000000000 would need gigabytes of memory.
Readiness probes cover applications that are loading large data or configuration files or waiting on external dependencies.
SQLite recursive triggers are enabled by default.
Well-normalized schemas rarely need more than about 100 columns.
MySQL's InnoDB uses Repeatable Read as its default isolation level.
SQLite BLOBs can be read incrementally with sqlite3_blob_open().
If a startup probe never succeeds, the container keeps running but is never marked ready.
A restarted Redis master with an empty dataset would wipe out its replicas' data.
To delay readiness checks during initialization you use initialDelaySeconds or the startup probe.
Kubernetes gRPC probes became generally available in Kubernetes 1.27.
PostgreSQL allows up to 1600 columns per table.
Within a Redis replication history the offset works as a logical clock.
After the background save, the Redis master transfers the RDB file and then the buffered commands to the replica.
Read-only Redis replicas are safe to expose to untrusted networks.
For simple single-row read-modify-write patterns, Read Committed with SELECT FOR UPDATE or advisory locks is often simpler and faster than Serializable.
Requiring at least N connected replicas guarantees that every Redis write reaches a replica.
If the master's backlog is too small or the replication history is no longer known, Redis performs a full resynchronization.
WAIT makes every Redis write durable.
PostgreSQL implements all four standard isolation levels as distinct behaviours.
A write that would grow an SQLite database past SQLITE_MAX_PAGE_COUNT returns SQLITE_FULL.
Transactions should be kept short under Serializable.
After a serialization failure, a PostgreSQL application should retry only the failed statement.
A SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE transaction never blocks.
failureThreshold * periodSeconds of the startup probe should cover the worst-case startup time.
Redis diskless replication has been enabled by default since version 7.0.
SQLite strings and BLOBs are capped at 1 billion bytes by default.
In gRPC TLS mode the kubelet verifies the server certificate.
SQLite allocates space for every host parameter number up to the largest one used.
